**Release workflow pins PyPI publish action to mutable branch reference** Release workflow pins PyPI publish action to mutable branch `release/v1`. Pin to a full 40-character commit SHA with a version comment.
AI prompt ```text Check if this security scanner issue is valid. If so, understand the root cause and fix it. If appropriate, update or add tests. Keep the change focused and preserve intended behavior. P0 Release workflow pins PyPI publish action to mutable branch reference `uses: pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish@release/v1` references a branch, not an immutable commit SHA. If the action repository is compromised, any malicious commit pushed to the `release/v1` branch is immediately executed in the release workflow, which has OIDC write permissions for PyPI trusted publishing. Pin to the full 40-character commit SHA of the action version you want, with a version comment: `uses: pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish@<sha> # release/v1` ```

**Release workflow lacks top-level permissions block** No top-level permissions block means the build job inherits default repo token permissions. Add `permissions: {}` at the workflow top level and grant per-job least privilege.
AI prompt ```text Check if this security scanner issue is valid. If so, understand the root cause and fix it. If appropriate, update or add tests. Keep the change focused and preserve intended behavior. P1 Release workflow lacks top-level permissions block The workflow does not declare a top-level `permissions:` block, so the default `GITHUB_TOKEN` permissions for the repository apply to the `build` job. On older repos or orgs with legacy defaults, this can grant `write-all` access to repository contents, issues, pull requests, and packages. Add `permissions: {}` at the top of the workflow and grant only the specific permissions each job needs (e.g., `contents: read` for the build job, `id-token: write` for the publish job). ```

**Workflow actions pinned to mutable tags instead of commit SHAs** Actions use mutable tag references that can be redirected to malicious commits. Pin every action to a full commit SHA with a version comment.
AI prompt ```text Check if this security scanner issue is valid. If so, understand the root cause and fix it. If appropriate, update or add tests. Keep the change focused and preserve intended behavior. P1 Workflow actions pinned to mutable tags instead of commit SHAs Multiple `uses:` lines reference mutable tags: `actions/checkout@v4` (line 11), `astral-sh/setup-uv@v5` (line 14), `actions/upload-artifact@v4` (line 23), and `actions/download-artifact@v4` (line 37). Tags can be force-pushed by an attacker who compromises the action repository, redirecting the tag to a malicious commit. Replace every tag reference with the full 40-character commit SHA of the intended version, followed by a `# vX.Y.Z` comment (e.g., `uses: actions/checkout@<sha> # v4.2.2`). ```

Prompt for AI agents (unresolved issues) ```text Check if these issues are valid — if so, understand the root cause of each and fix them. If appropriate, use sub-agents to investigate and fix each issue separately. P2: Consider adding a top-level `permissions` block (for example `permissions: {}`) so jobs do not inherit repository-default `GITHUB_TOKEN` scopes. As written, the `build` job runs with ambient defaults instead of explicitly minimal permissions. P1: Several action steps are pinned to mutable tags (`@v4`, `@v5`) rather than immutable commit SHAs. Pinning each `uses:` reference to a full SHA would harden the release pipeline against upstream tag retargeting. P0: Pin this PyPI publish action to a full commit SHA instead of `release/v1`. A branch ref is mutable, so a compromised upstream branch could change what runs in this trusted publishing step. P2: The example GitHub Pages workflow uses `uvx --from ics-to-static-site-themes` without pinning a version. Because this workflow runs on a daily schedule, each execution will pull the latest published package. An upstream release could change or break behavior even when the repository itself hasn't changed, undermining reproducibility — especially since this PR emphasizes deterministic builds with `--today` and `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH`. Consider pinning the package version in the example, e.g. `uvx --from ics-to-static-site-themes==0.4.2 ical-events ...`. ```
